title: staged-deserialization-and-idempotent-retries-for-python-sdk-streaming
creator: Priya Nair
description: Implement a robust staged deserialization model for the Python SDK that makes streaming LLM outputs ergonomic, retry-safe, and efficient. Goals: (1) let application code operate on lightweight, partially-hydrated objects during streaming (header/meta first, body later), (2) provide clear idempotency semantics so retries can safely reassemble chunks without double-processing, and (3) offer best-practice examples for pydantic v2 and dataclasses users that minimize allocations and maximize clarity. This ticket covers design, a reference implementation, unit + integration tests, and example notebooks for customers.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a StreamEnvelope type that separates metadata, incremental chunks, and final manifest
Partial-hydration API allows consumers to access metadata fields synchronously before body completes
Retry logic can reattach previously-received chunks and reconcile ordering without duplicating emitted events
Adapters provided for both pydantic v2 BaseModel and stdlib dataclasses that are documented and tested
End-to-end examples show <100ms overhead on median cases and graceful backpressure behavior under 95th percentile load
Pull request has automated tests and a migration note for existing streaming consumers
testing_plan: Unit tests for StreamEnvelope chunk reassembly, ordering invariants, and idempotent apply() semantics; integration tests against the streaming runtime simulator with injected duplicate/late/reordered chunks; benchmark harness that measures allocations and latency across pydantic/dataclass adapters; example notebook that runs against sandbox Redwood hosted endpoint with a small open model.
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag `staged_deserialize_v1`. Publish SDK beta to TestPyPI with the feature flag enabled by default for beta channel. Solicit feedback from 3 internal customers (console, dedicated, and examples) over two weeks. If no regressions, enable for 2025.03 minor release guarded by a migration note and a toggle in Console to fallback to legacy stream parsing.
